Anantara-branded villas in Bali up for sale with prices from US$700,000
article:
A collection of branded residences located in Bali, Indonesia, is up for grabs. Anantara Residences Ubud Bali launched for sale this month, offering 15 one- and two-bedroom pool villas.

Developed by Minor International (which owns the Anantara brand) and state-owned Indonesian developer PT Wijaya Karya Realty, the development neighbours Anantara Ubud Bali Resort, an 85-key hotel the partners opened in October 2024.

The resort and residences are located in Payangan, about 35 minutes north of central Ubud and two hours from Denpasar International Airport. The Payangan district is known for its picturesque highlands, river valleys and rainforests.

Indicative prices of the villas start from an estimated US$700,000 (around $895,000).

One-bedroom villas measure 1,163 sq ft. Each unit features a private infinity pool with views overlooking the forest.

Two-bedroom villas, each spanning 1,765 sq ft, also come with a private pool. Designed for families, they feature an expansive layout, along with en suite bathrooms in both bedrooms.

Jakarta-based architecture firm Aboday designed the villas, with interiors crafted by Malaysia’s EDC International.

The villas include 24-hour manned security, fibre-optic internet and underground utilities, emergency power supply, and rainwater recycling systems for landscaping.

Owners will have access to resort amenities, which include a spa, fitness centre, kids’ and teens’ clubs, and around-the-clock butler services.

Qualified owners will have the option to join the development’s resort-managed rental programme. Anantara will fully manage the property on behalf of owners, according to Minor International.

With a fully compliant rental model operated by Anantara, the development gives owners access to global demand, expert revenue management and hassle-free property care,” said Micah Tamthai, the group’s COO of lifestyle and real estate.

Tamthai believes the residences, designed for high-net-worth individuals, will appeal not only to investors but also to “wellness seekers and culture aficionados who want to live, not just visit, Bali”.

"We’re seeing strong local demand from Jakarta and Surabaya, as well as from buyers in Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, the US and the UK, all looking to diversify their portfolios with branded real estate in Southeast Asia," he said.

title: Ground-floor strata commercial unit on Keong Saik Road for sale at $11 mil
article:
A ground-floor strata commercial unit at 6 Keong Saik Road is being offered for sale through an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The 999-year leasehold unit measuring 1,389 sq ft is priced from $11 million, or $7,919 psf.

The unit is approved for restaurant use, according to Steward Asia (a unit of PropNex), which is marketing the property. French restaurant Loulou formerly occupied the unit, but it has ceased operations and vacated the space.

The unit sits on the ground floor of a strata-titled three-storey shophouse. It last changed hands for $8.5 million ($6,121 psf) in September 2024, based on lodged caveats.

The latest Keong Saik Road commercial transaction was for a freehold shophouse that fetched $16 million in June, caveats show. Before that, Steward Asia had brokered the deal for another freehold shophouse at 3 Keong Saik Road for $22 million in May.

“At $11 million, 6 Keong Saik Road gives investors a 999-year lease on the same street, with F&B approval already in place to attract tenants and owner-occupiers,” said Raelyn Lee, Steward Asia’s listing manager.

Steward Asia co-founder Loyalle Chin added that no freehold or 999-year shophouse in the CBD and Chinatown has sold below $15 million since 2025.

The EOI will close at 3pm on Oct 30.

title: Keppel DC REIT vs CICT: Which REIT Would I Buy Today?
article:

passive income from property
without buying any yourself.
Two of the best known, though, collect that income from two very different property types.
Keppel DC REIT
(SGX: AJBU), or KDCREIT, offers exposure to secular technology trends (AI and cloud computing) through its various
data centres
.
On the other hand,
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), or CICT, takes a more traditional route with malls, offices and integrated developments.
Let’s find out which one offers the better risk-reward balance today.

Understanding the Two REITs
As at 30 June 2026 (1H2026), KDCREIT owns 25 data centres across ten countries, with Singapore the biggest market at 62.8% of assets under management.
Internet companies are the main customers, supplying 70.4% of rental income.
Colocation leases, which bring in roughly 74% of the rent, last only 2.8 years on average, so renewals come around quickly.
Occupancy stands at 92.5%, but a tenant has vacated the Cardiff site, and without it the figure would be 95.3%.
Customers have already signed up for about 95% of its power capacity.
At renewal, rents rose by about 10% on average in 1H2026, and the REIT grew by buying or upgrading data centres.
Almost all of CICT’s portfolio is in Singapore.
At the end of 1H2026 (30 June 2026), 97.7% of retail space was occupied, against 94.4% of offices and 95.5% of integrated developments.
Its retail leases have a weighted average expiry of just 2.0 years, so CICT can reprice shop space regularly.
Rents on renewed retail leases rose 4.0%, and on office leases 6.5%, in 1H2026, supporting CICT’s distributable income.

Both raised DPU in 1H2026, by 11.3% at KDCREIT and 7.1% at CICT.
Since FY2021, though, CICT’s DPU has grown 11.3%, or 2.7% a year, and has risen every year.
KDCREIT grew about 1.3% a year, with a single decline, in 2023.
Neither REIT splits organic growth from acquisitions, but unit counts help.
KDCREIT’s unit count has risen substantially over the past few years as the REIT used equity to buy assets.
In 1H2026, its distributable income rose 18.5% but DPU only 11.3%.
Similarly, CICT issued new units to help fund its latest acquisition, Paragon.
Concentration matters for sustainability.
A single hyperscaler, meaning a very large cloud operator, supplies more than 40% of KDCREIT’s rental income.
Keppel DC Singapore 1 is a weak spot: it was only 46.5% occupied at 30 June 2026, and its contracts averaged just 1.1 years.
CICT’s largest tenant supplies 4.6% of rent, and its top ten tenants, 16%.

KDCREIT wins four of five measures, but its shorter 3.1-year average debt term means it will need to refinance its S$2.3 billion of debt sooner than CICT.
A 0.25-percentage-point rate change moves KDCREIT’s DPU by about 0.3%, roughly 1.2% for a full percentage point.
For CICT, a one-percentage-point rate rise would cut DPU by about S$0.0027, or around 2%.
In September 2026, KDCREIT agreed to buy stakes in two Tokyo data centres for about S$1.37 billion, partly funded by a S$625 million placement of new units at S$2.10 each.
Aggregate leverage is expected to rise from 34.0% to about 38.0%, just under its 40% internal leverage limit.
CICT funded Paragon with a S$750 million placement at S$2.30 a unit, debt, and the S$2.476 billion sale of Asia Square Tower 2.
Growth Potential: Data Centres vs Retail and Offices
KDCREIT has the stronger tailwind, with reversions of about 10% for 1H2026 and steady cloud and AI demand.
The risks are power supply, reliance on one large client, capital spending and shifts in AI workloads.
Faster distributable income growth likely needs acquisitions and, as the Tokyo deal shows, fresh equity.
CICT’s growth is slower but easier to see.
Paragon, bought at a 3.9% yield, adds about 1.7% to full-year DPU, with roughly half showing up in 2027.
Add organic growth of 1.5% to 2%, and DPU growth of about 2.5% in 2027 looks plausible.
Asset enhancement initiatives (AEIs) at Tampines Mall and Lot One could add an estimated 0.5% or so, based on their capex and expected returns.
Over the long term, KDCREIT has the higher ceiling thanks to its structural tailwind, but the REIT is dependent on power, a few clients and fresh equity.
CICT grows slowly from a diversified base.

KDCREIT trades 24% above NAV and CICT 3% above.
A premium can be justified by faster growth and a cleaner balance sheet, but it raises expectations.
KDCREIT’s DPU grew just 1.3% a year over four years, and part of the latest jump came from buying out the remaining stakes in Keppel DC Singapore 3 and 4, not just rent growth.
Higher interest costs on acquisition loans offset part of the gain.
Both trade near the bottom of their 52-week price ranges, so both yields sit near the top, CICT’s more so.
Total return is roughly yield plus
DPU growth
.
Assume yields stay put for three years.
If KDCREIT’s DPU grows 5% a year (well above its 1.3% track record) and CICT’s grows 3%, KDCREIT returns about 10% a year and CICT about 8.4%.
But KDCREIT trades at 1.24 times NAV.
If that premium shrinks to 1.10 times over three years, its return falls to about 6%, and it would need DPU growth of about 7% a year to keep pace with CICT.
At its historical growth rate, KDCREIT would trail CICT even if its premium held.
Get Smart: Which REIT Would I Buy Today?
KDCREIT’s case rests on its growth and its balance sheet, with 1H2026 DPU up 11.3% and leverage of 34%, rising to about 38% after the Tokyo deal.
CICT’s case rests on income and price, with a 5.42% yield and a DPU that has risen every year since FY2021.
Which REIT to buy depends on whether you’re comfortable trading lower income today for faster growth (KDCREIT), or prefer stable income diversified across multiple tenants and property types (CICT).

title: Qatar LNG cargo makes rare Red Sea journey to get gas to Europe
article:
(Oct 19): A carrier loaded with Qatari liquefied natural gas (LNG) is sailing north through the Red Sea, potentially speeding up delivery to European customers with a rare transit through waters vulnerable to renewed attacks from Houthi rebels.

The tanker, which loaded an LNG cargo in Qatar in August, is signalling Poland as its next destination, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Poland’s Orlen SA has a long-term supply contract with QatarEnergy, though shipments under the deal were cancelled after the exporter’s giant Ras Laffan plant was hit by drone strikes in March.

The transit — which comes as European natural gas prices hit the highest level in almost four years — is unusual. Commercial vessels have increasingly tended to take long detours to avoid the Red Sea, typically sailing around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope to head to Europe, a route that can add almost two weeks and extra costs to a one-way journey.

UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a security outfit which links commercial shipping and military forces, reported on Saturday that an unnamed LNG tanker was approached southeast of the Yemeni port of Al Mukalla, in the Gulf of Aden, by a skiff that fired two shots. The tanker’s security team fired two shots in return.

UKMTO did not provide further details, though ship-tracking data suggest the Poland-bound carrier was the only LNG tanker in the region at the time. The data suggests the vessel has since continued its journey.

QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

See also: Exxon signals record refining earnings on soaring diesel prices

Continued disruption around the Strait of Hormuz has tightened global LNG supply for months, driving up prices and forcing Middle Eastern suppliers to look for workarounds.

This latest Qatari cargo is heading to Europe at a time when the continent has struggled to refill its gas inventories ahead of winter. Reserves of the fuel are sitting at the lowest seasonal level in over a decade, threatening even higher prices as temperatures begin to drop.

title: JPMorgan brings deposit token to ethereum for institutional clients
article:
(Oct 19): JPMorgan Chase & Co is launching its deposit token on ethereum, extending the lender’s push into blockchain payments as Wall Street grows more comfortable moving money on public networks.

JPM Coin — which represents US dollar deposits at the largest US bank — will be made available to the company’s institutional clients on the ethereum network, JPMorgan said in a statement on Monday. First launched last year on Coinbase Global Inc-affiliated blockchain base, the deposit token allows clients to send and receive money in seconds and 24/7, rather than over several days and only during working hours.

The bank expects JPM Coin to be used by large clients in the cryptocurrency sector seeking a way to make payments on blockchain, as well as financial institutions that need a form of digital cash to settle or collateralise transactions of tokenised assets, Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview.

Tokenisation allows traditional assets such as stocks, bonds and funds to be represented and transferred via blockchain networks. While banks have spent more than a decade exploring the technology’s potential, a lot of the work to date has focused on private networks, where access is restricted and banks retain greater control over participants.

Moving onto public infrastructure — albeit with limits on who can hold the tokens — brings Wall Street closer to the crypto ecosystem, enabling them to tap into existing pools of liquidity and developer activity.

“We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto,” Landriault said. “It’s not just Wall Street going to public chains, but the institutional web3 players getting more embedded and partnering with traditional financial institutions.” JPM Coin’s move onto ethereum underscores that shift, she added.

See also: Crypto wallet tampering fallout widens as OneKey drops Malaysian reseller

The bank chose to bring the token to ethereum because of its liquidity and existing use among clients, Landriault said. Ethereum is the largest blockchain by the total value of assets locked into it, with about US$50 billion deposited in applications running on the network, according to DefiLlama data.

JPMorgan’s expansion comes as banks and other large financial firms seek ways to move assets faster and beyond the limitations of traditional systems by using crypto’s underlying technology. A company backed by more than 100 corporations including Visa Inc, Stripe Inc, and Mastercard Inc issued a US dollar-pegged stablecoin last month, another form of digital money.

JPMorgan is one of the more active banks in blockchain development. It also runs the Kinexys Blockchain Deposit Account network, which allows corporate clients to move dollars, euros, pounds and several other currencies, on the bank’s private blockchain. The network processes more than US$7 billion in transactions a day, JPMorgan said, a sliver of the roughly US$12 trillion a day its broader payments division handles daily.

title: Morgan Stanley enters UK savings market with Raisin partnership
article:
(Oct 19): Morgan Stanley is partnering with fintech platform Raisin UK to roll out savings accounts to individuals, following similar moves in Germany and the Netherlands.

Starting this week, the Wall Street bank is offering fixed-term deposits at interest rates as high as 5.1%, with a minimum deposit of £1,000 (US$1,334), the company said in a statement Monday. Over time, Morgan Stanley will look at other potential partners and products, according to people familiar with the matter.

The move is part of the bank’s deposit-gathering strategy and doesn’t reflect a wider push into UK consumer or retail banking, said the people, who asked not to be named as the details aren’t public.

“The UK is one of the world’s largest and most established savings markets,” Christopher Beatty, Morgan Stanley’s chief operating officer for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, said in a statement.

In the US, Morgan Stanley offers savings accounts to clients with brokerage accounts. In September, the bank entered the Netherlands via Raisin, following a similar partnership in Germany in 2025.

The UK savings market has been dominated by high street lenders including Lloyds Banking Group Plc and Nationwide Building Society, though Wall Street firms have entered the market in recent years.

See also: PHP agrees £700 mil UK private hospital venture with GIC

JPMorgan Chase & Co opened Chase in the UK in 2021 before expanding into savings products, then moving into Germany earlier this year. Goldman Sachs Group Inc’s retail bank Marcus started UK operations in 2018. Goldman has also begun hiring staff to assess the viability of launching Marcus in Ireland.

Morgan Stanley’s new offering compares to similar accounts at rivals such as Marcus, which offers a one-year fixed term account at 4.75%.

title: PHP agrees £700 mil UK private hospital venture with GIC
article:
(Oct 19): Primary Health properties Plc has formed a £700 million (US$933 million) venture with GIC Pte Ltd, part of its ongoing plan to reduce debt levels following a merger last year.

The UK healthcare landlord will seed the venture with 27 private hospitals, according to a statement Monday. As part of the deal, PHP will receive about £500 million, which will be used to repay the bridging loan it used to finance the takeover of rival Assura, and another debt facility. This will reduce PHP’s net debt to about £2.9 billion.

While Europe’s property markets continue to suffer in the face of high bond yields, infrastructure-like assets that have offer secure long-term income and can help hedge against inflation have been a relative bright spot. Demand for private healthcare in the UK has been increasing as pressure on public services grows, leading to lengthy delays for treatment.

“In addition to generating proceeds to reduce our borrowings, the transaction enhances returns on invested equity for our shareholders and brings a highly aligned capital partner to support investment in essential UK hospital infrastructure,” said Mark Davies, chief executive officer at PHP.

Last year, PHP outbid KKR & Co to buy Assura in a combination that created one of the UK’s largest publicly traded landlords. The listed real estate market has continued to shrink this year after Prologis Inc secured a deal to takeover the UK’s largest listed real estate company, Segro Plc.

Rothschild & Co acted as financial adviser to PHP.

See also: Vietnam plans index options for next year after FTSE upgrade

title: Dubai sweetens first IPO since war with US$592 mil dividend
article:
(Oct 19): DIP Holding PLC is trying to rustle up demand for the United Arab Emirates’ first initial public offering since the Iran war began by offering investors dividend payouts worth US$592 million over the next three years.

The firm’s sole owner, Dubai Investments PJSC, plans to sell 20% of the company’s shares, according to terms of the deal seen by Bloomberg News. DIP Holding owns Dubai Investments Park, one of the UAE’s largest mixed-use developments.

The subscription period will run from Oct 27 to Nov 3, with trading expected to start on Nov 11 on Dubai’s bourse. Bloomberg News reported the firm’s plans to start investor meetings last week.

Beyond DIP Holding, Dubai Investments has stakes in about 30 companies spanning manufacturing, real estate and financial services. Shares in the parent company rose as much as 5.1%, the most since early May.

The firm expects to pay annualised dividends of 700 million dirhams (US$190.58 million) in 2026, and 725 million dirhams and 750 million dirhams in 2027 and 2028 respectively.

The 2,300-hectare (8.9-square miles) DIP was established in 1997 and includes warehouses, hotels, retail outlets, schools and medical centres.

See also: Mi Material launches IPO at $1.80 each, aims to raise gross proceeds of $168.2 mil

Citigroup Inc, Emirates NBD Capital and HSBC Holdings Plc are the joint global coordinators on the deal, with Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Arqaam, Dubai Islamic Bank and EFG Hermes mandated as joint bookrunners.

Once a hub for IPOs, Gulf listing volumes have slumped this year as the regional war deepens a broader market slowdown. Equity markets across the region have fallen since the conflict began, with Oman the sole exception, while Dubai’s benchmark index is down about 9%.

title: Nidec legal reckoning reaches founder, shares hit decade low
article:
(Oct 19): Nidec Corp shares fell to their lowest in a decade after an outside committee concluded that founder Shigenobu Nagamori and other current or former executives bear civil liability for damages linked to years of improper accounting.

The finding, which was submitted to the board last week, deepens a crisis that has prompted the motor maker’s biggest shareholder to call for a review of privatisation options. Nidec plans to publish a partially redacted version of the report on Tuesday.

While the announcement marks a break with Nidec’s founder-dominated past, it also raises questions over whether the company’s cleanup effort still has a long way to go. The manufacturer is seeking to regain auditor approval and convince the Tokyo Stock Exchange that its internal controls have been repaired. At the same time, newly appointed chief executive officer Michio Kaida needs to restructure loss-making businesses and respond to activist pressure.

Nidec shares fell to their lowest since 2016 on Monday. The stock has lost more than a third of its value since late September, when Nidec announced the sudden exit of Mitsuya Kishida as CEO. The motor manufacturer now has a market value of ¥2.1 trillion ($17 billion), compared with almost ¥9 trillion less than six years ago.

Nidec said it recognised that multiple directors and other executives violated corporate laws and regulations while carrying out their duties and would consider claims for damages and other legal measures, then respond swiftly. The committee said the amount of any damages should be determined according to each person’s contribution.

Apart from Nagamori, the report on Friday named former CEOs Jun Seki and Kishida, former chairman Hiroshi Kobe, former President Hiroyuki Yoshimoto and former senior vice-president Akira Sato. Kazuya Murakami, identified by the committee as one of those bearing liability, was listed as the company’s chief legal officer and head of compliance as of Oct 1. Nidec said he is no longer employed at the company.

See also: BOJ to lean against back-to-back rate hike in October — Bloomberg

The scope of any damages to be claimed should be determined according to their degree of contribution, Nidec said in the statement. The latest finding could help Kaida demonstrate that Nidec’s board is willing to hold its former leaders accountable.

Nidec has been designated a security on special alert since October 2025 because of the need to improve its internal management system. Accounting auditor PwC Japan withheld its opinion on the accounts after saying it was unable to obtain sufficient and appropriate evidence. The company is seeking to obtain the auditor’s sign-off and submit a report to the exchange by Oct 28 as it seeks to avoid a delisting notice.

Oasis Management Co disclosed last week that its stake in Nidec had risen to 9%, making it the largest disclosed shareholder and placing it ahead of Nagamori’s direct holding. Oasis founder Seth Fischer has urged Nidec’s outside directors to hire financial advisers and seek preliminary, non-binding proposals as protection against an unintended delisting.

See also: Topix’s biggest ever revamp to cull hundreds of Japan stocks

Nagamori built Nidec through decades of aggressive acquisitions and a high-pressure operating culture, but struggled to hand over control. Yoshimoto and Seki were each tapped as potential successors before leaving, while Nagamori retained influence over the company. He relinquished his last formal title in February but remains one of Nidec’s largest shareholders.

The accounting fallout has devastated Nidec’s finances. It reported a ¥519 billion operating loss for the year ended March after recording a ¥632 billion impairment. The company forecast a return to ¥200 billion in profit on ¥2.8 trillion of sales in the current fiscal year.

The legal claims and ongoing uncertainty over the accounts and a potential delisting may also complicate a sale of the company. Any buyer would have to assess the legal claims, audit questions and whether Nagamori, who remains a major shareholder, would support any transaction.

title: Foxconn buys US$727 mil stake in Mitsubishi Electric unit making EV parts
article:
(Oct 19): Hon Hai Precision Industry Co is paying ¥115 billion (US$727 million) for a 50% stake in Mitsubishi Electric Corp’s automotive-components unit, with the goal of turning it into a business with more than ¥1 trillion in sales.

Mitsubishi will contribute technology in electric powertrains, autonomous driving and in-car intelligence for EV platforms developed by Hon Hai, better known as Foxconn, the companies said Monday during a news conference in Tokyo.

The tie-up gives Foxconn a deeper foothold in the auto industry as it pushes its contract-manufacturing model into EVs, while giving Mitsubishi Electric a partner to help scale its car-parts business. The companies plan to combine Mitsubishi’s long-standing relationships with automakers with Foxconn’s faster development model, while broadening the business beyond traditional auto components into EV and autonomous-driving platforms.

“What attracted us most was the electronic-control technology — and the substantial software resources behind them,” Jun Seki, Foxconn’s chief strategy officer for EVs, said at the event.

The deal values the new automotive business at ¥320 billion on an enterprise-value basis. The unit generated ¥876 billion in revenue and ¥54 billion in operating profit in the year ended March.

Mitsubishi Electric expects to book an impairment charge of about ¥100 billion this fiscal year as a result of the transaction. It plans to update its full-year earnings forecast on Oct 30.

See also: UniCredit gets ECB go-ahead to take control of Commerzbank

The companies expect the transaction to be completed in October 2027. The parts business will then become a 50-50 venture and cease to be a consolidated Mitsubishi Electric subsidiary.

title: Thailand targets US$417 mil of land in foreign buyer crackdown
article:
(Oct 19): Thailand is moving to force the sale of land worth about 14 billion baht (US$417 million or $530 million) as it cracks down on foreigners who evade an ownership ban by holding property via local proxies.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Monday that his government is stepping up investigations into such arrangements and tightening scrutiny of new purchases.

Foreigners are prohibited from owning land in Thailand, but some use Thai nominees to circumvent the restrictions, a practice under growing scrutiny after a series of cases in major tourist and business centres.

Authorities are targeting about 5,467 rai (2,161 acres) of land linked to suspected nominee arrangements, according to Somchai Leelanoy, director-general of the Department of Lands. That is an area roughly equivalent to 1,225 standard soccer fields.

Anutin ordered officials to accelerate investigations of high-risk cases by December and enforce laws requiring illegally held land to be sold. Authorities will also seek to prevent new nominee arrangements from entering the property system, he said at a briefing Monday.

The government is tightening checks on buyers as part of the effort. Individuals purchasing land for more than two million baht, or property with an assessed value exceeding five million baht, will face background checks, Somchai said.

See also: Bukit Sembawang to acquire Kallang Distripark land from other Lee-family entities for $196 mil

Thai nationals married to foreigners will have to show that money used to purchase land belongs to the Thai spouse. Companies buying property will face scrutiny of their shareholders and sources of funds and be required to provide supporting documents under Thailand’s land laws.

title: Malaysia's September exports surge to five-year high on AI demand
article:
(Oct 19): Malaysia’s exports surged to its highest level in more than five years in September as the trade-dependent nation continues to benefit from demand for artificial intelligence-related products.

Exports rose 54.5% in September from a year earlier, the highest since April 2021, and exceeding the 39.9% estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

The growth was boosted by higher exports of electrical and electronic products, valued at RM45 billion (US$11 billion) in September, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said in a statement Monday.

Shipments to the US surged 89.9%, and exports to China were up 22.1% for the month, according to the department.

Imports rose 52.7% in September from a year ago, higher than the 39% forecast in a Bloomberg survey.

Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM33.7 billion in September, above the RM31.6 billion surplus in the Bloomberg survey.

See also: Malaysia's King Sultan Ibrahim acquires 2.25% in Southern Alliance Mining in $6.1 mil offmarket deal

Demand for electronics used in AI have helped cushion Malaysia from global disruptions. The Southeast Asian country’s economy expanded 5.3% in the three months through September from a year earlier.

Exports in the third quarter rose 46%, the statistics department said. Malaysia’s total trade increased 30.1% from January to September compared to the same period a year ago, with exports up 34%.

The country’s consumer prices were up 1.8% in September from a year earlier, below the 1.9% forecast in a Bloomberg survey, according to separate data from the statistic department on Monday.

title: Vietnam plans index options for next year after FTSE upgrade
article:
(Oct 19): Vietnam aims to introduce stock index options in the first quarter of next year as the country seeks to deepen its capital markets and attract more overseas investors following an upgrade to its equity market.

Testing of contracts tied to the VN30 Index is scheduled for November and December, Vu Thi Thuy Nga, general director of the Hanoi Stock Exchange, said in an interview. The gauge comprises the 30 largest stocks by market value on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange.

The new derivatives products are being introduced to lure more foreign capital into Vietnamese shares after FTSE Russell upgraded the country to secondary emerging-market status from frontier effective last month. The reclassification is expected to broaden Vietnam’s access to global emerging-market investment, even as the transition is phased in, with inclusion in FTSE’s emerging-market indexes expected through 2027.

The authorities expect the new options to help increase trading activity and improve liquidity, potentially supporting broader participation in the market, Hanoi Stock Exchange’s Nga said.

“This is a highly anticipated product, and it is hoped that it will help the market take off,” she said. “Now that we have been upgraded, we need products that align with those of more developed exchanges.”

See also: Australia regulator halts another credit fund amid crackdown

Vietnam has undertaken a number of reforms in recent years to improve market accessibility.

Authorities have removed pre-funding requirements for equity trades, advanced plans for a centralised clearing system by 2027 and allowed foreign investors to trade via global brokerages, among other measures. The country is also weighing plans to allow trading during the midday break and widen daily price bands to improve liquidity.

The VN30 Index gained 5.9% in August amid optimism over the FTSE update before dropping 3.8% in September.
